title: Raise a loaded sit-stand desk converter: squeeze both side paddles, lift it along its arc, lock both sides in one notch
instruction: The sit-stand desk converter on the table is locked at its fourth setting with a monitor on its top and a keyboard on its tray. Raise it to its ninth setting, where the work surface is level with the top of the green card: take the handle at each side, squeeze both release paddles together, lift the top along its arc to that setting, release both paddles there so that both locks drop into the same notch, then let go and move both arms back. Nothing on it may fall.
context: Desk-top sit-stand converters such as the VariDesk Pro Plus 30 are common in offices and home offices, and their users raise and lower them several times a day. The maker's patent for the mechanism (US 10,413,053) gives each side its own lock: a handle pulls an anchor out of a row of holes in that side's pivot arm. The top is one rigid platform, so one anchor left in holds it: both handles must be squeezed together, about 70 cm apart, which one hand cannot do. A spring carries most of the weight; the hands release, lift and steer the top along its forward arc, then release together at the chosen notch. A hand that lets go early drops its pin into the next notch the top meets and stops it short.
setup: Units mm. Station frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers (94 mm opening, about 30 N per finger), bases at (0, +305) and (0, -305). 1) A VariDesk Pro Plus 30 sit-stand desk converter (Vari; 762 wide, 756 deep including its keyboard tray, 610 x 610 steel base, 11 settings, work surface 114 to 445 above the desk, 21 kg, rated 15.9 kg). It stands with its keyboard tray toward the robot. The base is centred on y = 0, from x = 289 to x = 899; its back edge is under the back of the work surface at the lowest setting. Work surface height at settings 1 to 11: 114, 162, 208, 253, 294, 331, 365, 393, 416, 433, 445. Going from setting 4 to setting 9, the work surface moves 172 toward the robot. Each lock's pin has 1.1 mm of side play in its notch (0.67 degrees of arm angle), and the loaded top rests on the low side of it: 3.8 mm below the heights above at setting 4, 1.8 mm at setting 9. 2) Start: locked at setting 4, resting in the notch. Work surface 249 above the table; front edge of the upper tier at x = 422, front edge of the keyboard tray at x = 104, tray surface 89 below the work surface. Each handle's release paddle (70 x 37 x 10, black plastic) sits 20 below the board's underside, centred 45 behind the upper tier's front edge and 29 in from its side edge. Paddle centres at the start: (467, +352, 205) and (467, -352, 205). 3) Load: a 24 in office monitor on its own stand, 4.0 kg (foot 220 x 180, panel 540 wide, 325 high, 45 deep, screen toward the robot). Its foot is centred on the work surface 95 behind the surface's middle, at station (736, 0). A full-size wired keyboard, 440 x 135 x 25, 0.6 kg, lies centred on the tray at station (258, 0). 4) A green card, 60 wide and 416 tall (the work surface's height at setting 9), stands upright on the table at (800, -420), right of the converter. Same layout every trial. Reset: squeeze both paddles, lower the top to setting 4 and release.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial. In a real trial: count the notches or measure the work surface's height (table above) against the green card, check each side's lock on its own (below), photograph the load against marks made at the start, and watch the video. In the simulation the same quantities are read from the lift joint, the two latches, the loads' poses and the arms' contacts, every 50 ms. Settings are read as a decimal number from the work surface's height on the table above (the simulation converts the arm angle the same way). A seated top reads about 0.09 below its notch (the pins' play), so the thresholds sit 0.3 below the notch: 0.2: at some moment the reading was 4.7 or more, i.e. the top reached setting 5 (both locks were open together; with a lock in, the play allows at most 4.09). 0.5: at the end the reading is 6.7 or more, i.e. setting 7 or higher, locked or not. 0.8: at the end both locks are seated in the same notch, setting 9 (reading 8.7 to 9.3), and the top is level (the two side edges' heights differ by at most 5 mm, ruler). 1.0: in addition the monitor and the keyboard have each moved at most 30 mm on their surfaces and tilted at most 10 degrees, and for the last second both grippers are off the converter and its load, each at least 50 mm from its handle. 0 for the whole trial if the monitor or the keyboard falls (tilts past 45 degrees or drops off its surface). Each lock is checked separately, because one seated lock alone holds the rigid top. A side's lock is seated when its release paddle has dropped fully back: its gap to the board is 20 mm (ruler, within 2 mm). A pin left on a tooth holds its paddle 14 mm or more higher. The simulation reads the same paddle height. Confirm by squeezing one paddle alone and pressing the top down: it must not move (the other side's lock holds); then swap sides. A top between notches, or with either paddle not fully down, is not locked. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lower the top to setting 4 (squeeze both paddles, press down, release), put the monitor and keyboard back on their marks.
fidelity: Isaac Lab, PhysX 240 Hz, true size. One articulation tree: the parallelogram lift is an arm plus a mimic-coupled top that stays level on the real arc. The counterbalance is a stated torsion spring (no published figure). Each paddle lifts only its own pin out of 11 notches. Locks, jams, grasps and loads act by contact only. Base fixed to the table. Display meshes over invisible box colliders. Handle, lock and spring numbers are estimates (README).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the arms moved above and in front of the converter and never touched it); demo: 1.0 (scripted, 575 steps: both paddles squeezed together, lifted, both locks seated in notch 9, load undisturbed)
